description:
FILED s525 (Fable, 2026-10-24) from the USER-asked parser review, docs/parser-review-s525.md.  NOTHING here starts before the USER rules on review Â§5 (spike first vs Option 1; BEGIN/use running at transpile time; the perl floor).

THE SPIKE (recommended, 2-3 Opus sessions, a measurement table as the deliverable, zero production code):
  S1 op census: a B walker (B::main_root / B::walkoptree, no Concise text parsing) over the four populations (perl-tests/*.t, perl suite t/, everyday/, cpan-tests dists) under 5.40.3 -- distinct ops, frequency, cumulative coverage ("N ops cover 95 % of occurrences"), the long tail by name.
  S2 version delta: the same census under the local perlbrew 5.32.1 and 5.26.3 builds -- which ops differ (multiconcat 5.28, padsv_store 5.38, cmpchain 5.32, class ops 5.38, argcheck/argelem 5.26) and how many conditionals an emitter carries per supported floor (Ubuntu 22.04 = 5.34, 24.04 = 5.38).
  S3 BEGIN-hazard census: BEGIN bodies and import-time code in the four populations doing anything but use / @INC / $| / plan / chdir t -- count and kinds, so decision (1) is taken on numbers.  Method: B::save_BEGINs + walk begin_av, or a text pre-pass; prefer the former.
  S4 vertical slice: emit CLForm for the ~40 commonest ops onto the EXISTING runtime vocabulary (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp 174 exports) and run the everyday programs that fit end to end; calibrates lines-per-op and proves the op-to-runtime fit (pad -> let/cell mapping, nextstate -> line/package/hints, context flags -> the wantarray protocol).
  S5 eval seam: compile an eval string unrun with a synthetic pad (sub { my ($x, @list); sub { BODY } }) and map its OUTER padname entries onto the capture alist; one probe file, five shapes (scalar/array/hash capture, a my-shadow inside the eval, a nested sub).
  BAR: the table + a recalibrated session estimate for Option 3 (review Â§4 says 40-60 +-50 %); the USER decides.

IF THE USER TAKES OPTION 1 INSTEAD: order 1c (the binder = pad.c in Perl; Direction A of docs/var-handling-review-s379.md Â§3 with pad.c's exact rule: visible from the statement AFTER the declaration, OUTER = capture) -> 1a (ONE expect-state repair pass replacing the ~35 PPI repairs and all 18 re-serialize-and-reparse sites; the PPI-class x expect-state table read off toke.c's yyl_* handlers; re-lex a contradicting span with PPI::Tokenizer = the fragment_doc pattern) -> 1b (ONE keyword-class table from prototype("CORE::name") + a ~30-name syntax-keyword table, ONE extent rule per class from perly.y: FUNC takes its parens, UNIOP one term up to the comparison level, LSTOP a list to the next same-level or/and/xor or ")", FUN0 nothing; a user sub takes its prototype's class).  Bars in numbers: passes 69 -> <= 30; re-parse sites 18 -> 0; repair passes ~35 -> 1; scope-walk implementations 18 -> 1; handle_subcalls 1,811 -> < 600 lines; Math::BigInt::Calc transpile 3.7 s -> < 1.5 s; corpus-diff IDENTICAL per step, sweep TOTAL +0.

RESIDUES (either route; comment / table hygiene, none a silent-wrong):
  r1 three stale docs/ppi-upstream-bugs.md section citations in repair comments: _restore_signature_gid says Â§24 (is Â§32), _brace_glob_slot_symbol Â§24 (is Â§27), _repair_term_initial_complement Â§20 (is Â§21).
  r2 Pl/PExpr/Config.pm known_no_of_params: -11 and -12 both mean "one argument before a list" and no consumer distinguishes them (no == -11 / == -12 test anywhere); fold on the next touch.
  r3 Pl/Parser.pm is the shared pre-pass / facts layer under the deleted pipeline's name (~190 sub definitions in its 90-day diffs; feature_regions_of, strict_refs_regions_of, use_statements_of, _extract_module_prototypes, fragment_doc live there); 39 statements per module still lower through its TEXT seam (_fallback_stmt -> capture_v1 -> CLForm::raw: every use/require, every for/while/until-modifier statement, BEGIN, use constant).  Rename the live halves (PrePass / Facts) and give the four statement kinds a structured lowering.
  r4 _ppi_parse builds NINE PPI documents for one 2,566-line module (the file, its re-parse, the used modules read for prototypes, interpolation fragments); PPI::Node::find is 9,779 calls = 46 % of compile time -- the binder (1c) is the fix, not a cache.

MEASUREMENTS BEHIND THE NUMBERS (reproducible): NYTProf on ./pl2cl < lib/Math/BigInt/Calc.pm (3.74 s real); perl -MO=Deparse,-p of the repaired spellings; the pad probe (B main_cv->PADLIST, COP_SEQ_RANGE_LOW/HIGH, PADNAMEf_OUTER); perl 5.40.3 source at ~/perl5/perlbrew/build/perl-5.40.3/ (toke.c; PL_expect states in perl.h:5912; perly.y precedence 123-155, term rules 1095-1400; pad.c).
